"""Weekly sales dashboard figures drawn with seaborn (Agg backend)."""
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
import seaborn as sns  # noqa: E402


def frame(rows):
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def visits_vs_sales(df):
    """Number of points on the visits/sales scatter."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    sns.scatterplot(df["visits"], df["sales"], ax=ax)
    n = len(ax.collections[0].get_offsets())
    plt.close(fig)
    return n


def daily_means(df):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    sns.barplot(x="day", y="sales", data=df, ci=None, ax=ax)
    heights = [round(bar.get_height(), 2) for bar in ax.patches]
    plt.close(fig)
    return heights


def sales_histogram(df):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    sns.distplot(df["sales"], kde=False, bins=4, ax=ax)
    counts = [int(bar.get_height()) for bar in ax.patches]
    plt.close(fig)
    return counts


def density_filled(df):
    """Whether the density curve is drawn as a filled area."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    sns.kdeplot(df["sales"], shade=True, ax=ax)
    filled = len(ax.collections) > 0
    plt.close(fig)
    return filled

"""Per-shop small multiples (figure-level seaborn functions)."""
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import seaborn as sns  # noqa: E402


def trend_panels(df):
    """One regression panel per shop; returns the panel titles."""
    grid = sns.lmplot(x="visits", y="sales", col="shop", data=df, size=3)
    titles = [ax.get_title() for ax in grid.axes.flat]
    plt.close(grid.fig)
    return titles


def shop_counts(df):
    """Rows per shop, read back from a count plot."""
    grid = sns.factorplot(x="shop", data=df, kind="count")
    counts = [int(bar.get_height()) for bar in grid.ax.patches]
    plt.close(grid.fig)
    return counts

def daily_spread(df):
    """Length of each day's standard-deviation error bar."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    sns.barplot(x="day", y="sales", data=df, ci="sd", ax=ax)
    spans = []
    for line in ax.lines:
        low, high = line.get_ydata()
        spans.append(round(float(high - low), 3))
    plt.close(fig)
    return spans

notes: Old: seaborn 0.11.2 with matplotlib 3.6.3, pandas 1.5.3, numpy 1.26.4 on Python 3.11. New: seaborn 0.13.2 (the current release) with matplotlib 3.10.9, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.3.5 on Python 3.12: a real seaborn upgrade moves its companions too, and the toy only uses their stable APIs (DataFrame construction, subplots, artist getters). Seaborn functions return Axes/FacetGrid objects, so every value the tests read comes back through matplotlib getters (Rectangle.get_height, Line2D.get_ydata, Axes.get_title): the change scenario's ddof change is visible only at matplotlib.lines.Line2D.get_ydata, never at a seaborn symbol. Palettes, plotting_context and axes_style were compared between the two versions and are identical, so no seaborn call returns a changed value directly. kdeplot(shade=) gives no warning on 0.11.2 (FutureWarning only from 0.12). Not covered: violinplot(scale=), pointplot(join=), FacetGrid(size=), the 0.13 categorical rewrite's artist counts (barplot with hue adds legend patches to ax.patches). kdeplot runs scipy.stats.gaussian_kde on the old side (scipy is a seaborn 0.11 requirement; the new env has no scipy and seaborn 0.13 falls back to its own KDE): scipy's gaussian_kernel_estimate is a fused Cython function that is indexed (gaussian_kernel_estimate[spec]), so a capture that replaces compiled functions with plain wrappers breaks it (TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable, seen with pymolt 0.2 on 3.11 and 3.12).
